To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) primary creep can have significant effects on the stress and strain in the solder joint; (2) primary creep is more important for Sn3.8 Ag0.7 Cu than Sn40Pb; and (3) the effect of primary creep on the stress and the strain in the solder depends strongly on the thermal profile.
the role of plastic strain in solder joint fatigue life is negligible, and primary creep must be included for SnAgCU solder joints to accurately model the stress and strain in the solder joints.
primary creep is a major contributor to creep strain in SnPb and to a lesser extent in SnAgCu solder, and that the contribution is highly sensitive to thermal profile and ramp rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a methodology to assess the relative contributions of the different inelastic mechanisms (plasticity and creep) to the overall inelastic deformation of solder joints under thermal loading.
the effects of primary and secondary creep on the thermo-mechanic fatigue life prediction of solder joints.
the development of a methodology for the accurate modeling of thermal fatigue in solder joints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
primary creep is not negligible for SnPb solder joints under the conditions considered in this paper and that the effect of plasticity on the solder joint behavior is negligible.
primary creep strain should be considered for SnPb solder joints and that secondary creep strain should be the only creep strain considered for SnAgCu solder.
primary creep should be included in the analysis, and that its effect is dependent on the solder alloy and the thermal profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for SnPb, primary creep is significant and should be considered in the analysis of solder joints, while for SnAgCu it is less significant.
for trilayer SnAgCu and SnPb solder joint structures, the primary creep strain is significant and cannot be neglected.
the inclusion of primary creep in the modeling of SnPb is less critical than for the modeling of SnAgCu, particularly for high temperature amplitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative contributions of primary creep and secondary creep to total creep strain are highly dependent on the temperature profile and the ramp rate.
for thermal fatigue simulations of SnPb, primary creep can be neglected, but for SnAgCu primary creep must be included in the analysis.
primary creep cannot be ignored when modeling solder joint fatigue, and the magnitude of the error in the predicted stress/strain and life is a function of the thermal cycle profile.
